item.title: U.S. says it thwarted Iranian missile attack on troops in Middle East
item.description: Iran launched multiple ballistic missiles at U.S. forces in the Middle East in what U.S. Central Command described as an "attempted surprise attack" on Tuesday.

item.title: Swaths of damage as tornado tears through Wisconsin
item.description: Trees and power lines collapsed around cars as a tornado with winds of 140 miles per hour tore through central Wisconsin on Monday. The National Weather Service found a 12-mile-long swath of damage. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: New video shows Tony Romo's arrest in Wisconsin on suspicion of driving while intoxicated
item.description: The video shows Romo being pulled over, getting out of the Jeep he was driving and later undergoing field sobriety tests.

item.title: Back-to-school shopping to cost Americans roughly 11% more per child this year, report shows
item.description: New research from Groundwork Collaborative and the Century Foundation shows that U.S. parents can expect to spend close to $4,000 more per child on school supplies this year. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has the story.

item.title: Tornadoes pose bigger risk to homeowners than hurricanes, new research says
item.description: Jeremy Porter, chief economist at First Street, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss new research from his firm showing that severe convective storms that bring tornadoes, hail, and wind pose a bigger risk to homeowners than hurricanes.

item.title: Inside the Saudi-Houthi conflict as fighting between the sides heats up
item.description: The ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters is escalating amid a new wave of attacks. CBS News' Courtney Kealy breaks down what it means.

item.title: Nationwide American Airlines ground stop lifted after IT outage
item.description: American Airlines says its flights are resuming after an IT outage led to a temporary nationwide ground stop on Tuesday. CBS News senior transportation correspondent Kris Van Cleave has the latest.

item.title: American Airlines nationwide ground stop lifted after IT outage disrupts flights
item.description: According to the Air Traffic Control System Command Center, all airports and facilities were being impacted by the IT outage.

item.title: The funeral for Sen. Lindsey Graham | Special Report
item.description: Funeral services were held for Sen. Lindsey Graham Tuesday at the National Cathedral in Washington, D.C. Graham died July 11 after suffering an aortic dissection as a result of heart disease. He was 71. Major Garrett anchored CBS News' special report on the funeral.

item.title: Rep. Ro Khanna calls for a "Marshall Plan for America" to fight wealth inequality
item.description: Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna of California is beginning what he's calling the "New Economic Patriotism" tour Tuesday in his birthplace of Pennsylvania. Khanna joins "The Takeout" to discuss this and more.

item.title: What to know about the release of Fauci's diary entries, upcoming Senate testimony
item.description: Republican Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky has released more than a thousand pages of COVID-era journal entries from Dr. Anthony Fauci ahead of a scheduled Senate hearing with Fauci on Wednesday. CBS News' Arden Farhi breaks it down.

item.title: Japan quake kills at least 5; more trapped in collapsed mall, factory
item.description: A major earthquake in Japan's southwest killed at least five people and left dozens more injured or missing after a shopping center and a paper mill were heavily damaged

item.title: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed clarifies he didn't call opponent an "ogre"
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Dr. Abdul El-Sayed on Monday addressed a controversial comment that some assumed was directed at Rep. Haley Stevens, his primary opponent. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Trump calls Graham "beloved friend" and "American original" in eulogy
item.description: President Trump delivered the eulogy for friend and ally Sen. Lindsey Graham, who died unexpectedly just a short time after visiting Ukraine earlier this month.

item.title: Storms batter Northeast, triggering travel delays
item.description: More than 50 million people are at risk of flash flooding as storms batter the Northeast. The storms unleashed a nightmare chain reaction of airport backlogs at the peak of the summer travel season. Lilia Luciano reports and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Inflation topped 4% in May as CPI surged to highest level in 3 years
item.description: The Consumer Price Index rose last month at a 4.2% annual rate amid a spike in U.S. energy prices.

item.title: Why have tomato prices surged nearly 40% in a year?
item.description: Experts point to several factors, from tariffs to weather, behind the rapid price increase in the humble tomato.

item.title: Inflation held steady in February before Iran war drove up gas prices
item.description: The inflation data captures the period before the Iran war broke out. Since then, oil prices have surged, driving inflation fears.

item.title: 3 charts highlight the affordability issues Americans worry about most
item.description: President Trump touted his work during his first year back in office, saying, "inflation is plummeting, incomes are rising fast, the roaring economy is roaring like never before."

item.title: CPI rose at an annual rate of 2.4% in January, cooler than expected
item.description: Inflation came in below economists' forecasts and slowed from December's 2.7% annual rate.

item.title: Chew on this: U.S. food prices are up 19% since 2022
item.description: Food prices in December saw their biggest jump in more than three years, data shows, while the cost of eating out has also risen.

item.title: CPI rose at 2.7% annual rate in December as inflation remains sticky
item.description: Although there are signs that inflation is starting to ease, consumers still face pressures from high food prices and other costs.

item.title: 5 charts that illustrate America's deepening affordability crisis
item.description: Although inflation has eased, many Americans say they still feel squeezed financially. Here are five areas where households are feeling the pinch.

item.title: Wholesale turkey prices soar ahead of Thanksgiving. Here's why.
item.description: Wholesale prices for frozen turkeys are expected to be $1.32 per pound this year, a 40% increase from last year's average.

item.title: CPI report shows inflation continued to climb in September
item.description: Inflation last month rose at an annual rate of 3%, coming in below economists' forecasts as the impact of President Trump's tariffs remain muted.

item.title: CPI rose at a rate of 2.9% in August as U.S. inflation ticked higher
item.description: Today's CPI report marks the last major piece of economic data before the Federal Reserve's Sept. 17 rate decision meeting.

item.title: Inflation is creeping higher, putting pressure on American consumers
item.description: The Consumer Price Index likely inched higher in August, reflecting higher costs for food and other items, economists say.

item.title: Tracking cost of cars, trucks, groceries as Trump announces new tariffs
item.description: CBS News is tracking the rising cost of products most impacted by tariffs already imposed​ and new ones announced by President Trump, from grocery items to cars and trucks.

item.title: CPI rose in June to 2.7% annual rate, highest since February
item.description: The Consumer Price Index in June rose 2.7% on an annual basis, in line with economists' predictions.

item.title: Beef prices in the U.S. are searingly high. Here's why.
item.description: Beef costs around the U.S. surged to a record high in May. What's driving that jump, and are prices likely to ease up?
